_comment: Issue #279 item 1 — per-service RabbitMQ users/permissions. Loaded via load_definitions (docker-compose: rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf; Aspire: bind mount, see AppHost.cs). DEV-ONLY password hashes — regenerate with rabbitmq/generate-password-hashes.py if you change a dev password in .env.example / AppHost/appsettings.json. Never reuse these hashes/passwords outside local dev.

permissions._comment: exam-outbox-publisher: relays worksheet-DB outbox rows via IPublishEndpoint.Publish — never binds/consumes anything, so it only ever needs configure (exchange.declare) + write (basic.publish) on its own message-type exchanges, never read. Exchange name format is MassTransit's default RabbitMQ formatter: '<Namespace>:<TypeName>' (colon, not dot) — verified no SetEntityNameFormatter/custom MessageTopology override in the codebase. List matches OutboxEventRegistry entries actually written by api/ExamApp.Api.

identity-outbox-publisher: relays auth-api's identity-DB outbox rows. Only LoginAttemptedEvent/UserPreferredLocaleChangedEvent are ever written there (auth-api/Controllers/AuthController.cs). Publisher only — no read.

badge-outbox-publisher: relays BadgeService's badge-DB outbox rows. Only StudentPointsChangedEvent is written there (Services/BadgeService/Services/StudentPointsOutbox.cs) — this is the ONLY user allowed to configure/write that exchange, closing the fake-StudentPointsChangedEvent risk from issue #279. Publisher only — no read.

BadgeService (exam-badge-api): consumes everything except StudentPointsChangedEvent on its own 'badge-service' queue (Services/BadgeService/Program.cs ReceiveEndpoint; badge-service_error/_skipped are MassTransit's fault/skip queue+exchange for this endpoint — no explicit PublishFaults/Fault<T> publish configured, only UseMessageRetry, so no MassTransit.Fault:* exchange access is needed). RabbitMQ binding semantics: exchange.declare/queue.declare need 'configure'; binding a message-type exchange (source) to this endpoint's own exchange (destination), and this endpoint's own exchange (source) to its queue (destination), needs 'write' on the destination + 'read' on the source. Consumers must NEVER get 'write' on message-type exchanges — that would let them publish/forge events, not just consume them. So: configure = own queue/exchange/error/skipped + every message-type exchange it binds (to declare them); write = own queue/exchange/error/skipped ONLY; read = same as configure (it needs to read from the message exchanges as bind source, and its own queue to actually consume).

exam-dotnet-api: consumes only StudentPointsChangedEvent on its own 'exam-api' queue (api/ExamApp.Api/Program.cs ReceiveEndpoint, issue #225). Same binding semantics as badge_service above: write is restricted to its own queue/exchange/error/skipped, never the message-type exchange — it can read (subscribe to) StudentPointsChangedEvent but can never publish/forge one, and it has zero permission on any other event exchange (AnswerSubmittedEvent, TeacherApplicationDecidedEvent, etc.).
